p: Earth Observatory In the late 1800s, wildlife conservationists in New Zealand were recognizing how predators such as

, brought to the country to control other nonnative animal populations, were becoming a threat to native birds. Naturalists at the time surmised that some of the nation’s islands could serve as sanctuaries where endemic species could persist, free from the voracious newcomers.
Resolution Island, located in the Fiordland region along the rugged southwest edge of New Zealand’s South Island, was one of the first eyed for this purpose. Conservationist Thomas Henry Potts
that the island could be a place where “wingless species, and birds of feeble powers of flight, might there find a refuge for some of their representatives.”
So began an early systematic effort to protect kiwi,
, and other native birds on Resolution Island, the largest of the approximately 90 islands in
. This image, acquired with the
(Operational Land Imager) on
on December 12, 2025, shows the island’s setting amid a landscape of steep-sided valleys carved by glaciers and now inundated by the ocean.
The uninhabited island rises from sea level to the summit of Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters (3,507 feet). Its diverse habitats and
range from bogs and wetlands near the coast to widespread
at middle elevations to
in the subalpine and alpine areas. Offshore, the
protects estuarine and wave-exposed rocky reef habitats at the entrance to Dusky Sound, east of Five Fingers Peninsula.
Farther into the sound, Pigeon Island was the onetime home of Richard Henry, who was named caretaker of Resolution Island after it was designated a reserve in 1891. In what some have called a “
,” Henry spent years transporting more than 700 birds, mostly kiwi and kākāpō, by rowboat to Resolution and other would-be island sanctuaries nearby.
In 1900, however, people began spotting

on Resolution. It turns out the island is within swimming distance for animals such as stoats. Henry was intent on trapping the interlopers but eventually abandoned the project and moved on to caretaking work on another island. The spirit of his efforts lives on, though. A Department of Conservation program
aims to control stoat populations and bolster native species on Resolution.
